avoid_supplements.name: Nephrotoxic herbs (Aristolochia, Creatine megadoses)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Additive renal toxicity; valganciclovir is renally eliminated and can cause nephrotoxicity
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; monitor serum creatinine and BUN regularly

avoid_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
avoid_supplements.mechanism: May induce hepatic metabolism and reduce valganciclovir efficacy
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid or use alternative antidepressant; consult prescriber if concurrent use necessary

caution_supplements.name: Probiotics
caution_supplements.mechanism: Valganciclovir can disrupt gut flora; probiotics may help restore balance
caution_supplements.action: May be beneficial; use standard formulations and monitor GI tolerance

caution_supplements.name: Electrolyte supplements (Sodium, Potassium)
caution_supplements.mechanism: Valganciclovir may affect electrolyte balance; monitoring recommended
caution_supplements.action: Use only as directed by provider; monitor serum electrolytes

avoid_foods.name: High-dose vitamin C supplements in food form
avoid_foods.mechanism: May increase urinary crystallization risk; valganciclovir already poses renal risk
avoid_foods.action: Limit to RDA levels; ensure adequate hydration (2-3 L/day minimum)

caution_foods.name: Grapefruit/grapefruit juice
caution_foods.mechanism: Minimal CYP3A4 interaction as valganciclovir undergoes limited hepatic metabolism
caution_foods.action: No strict restriction needed, but monitor for any unexpected efficacy changes

caution_foods.name: High-sodium foods
caution_foods.mechanism: May affect renal function and electrolyte balance during valganciclovir therapy
caution_foods.action: Moderate sodium intake; maintain consistent dietary pattern

monitoring_notes: Monitor renal function (serum creatinine, GFR, BUN) at baseline and regularly during therapy as valganciclovir is nephrotoxic and renally eliminated. Ensure adequate hydration and assess for signs of nephrotoxicity (elevated creatinine, decreased urine output), electrolyte abnormalities, and bone marrow suppression.
